vulnerability.title: Add nodev Option to /dev/shm
vulnerability.description: The nodev mount option can be used to prevent creation of device files in /dev/shm. Legitimate character and block devices should not exist within temporary directories like /dev/shm. Add the nodev option to the fourth column of /etc/fstab for the line which controls mounting of /dev/shm.
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if ( ! ( { rpm --quiet -q kernel-core ;} && { rpm --quiet -q rpm-ostree ;} && { rpm --quiet -q bootc ;} && { ! rpm --quiet -q openshift-kubelet ;} && ([ -f /run/ostree-booted ] || [ -L /ostree ]) ) && ! ( [ -f /.dockerenv ] || [ -f /run/.containerenv ] ) ); then function perform_remediation { mount_point_match_regexp="$(printf "^[[:space:]]*[^#].*[[:space:]]%s[[:space:]]" /dev/shm)" # If the mount point is not in /etc/fstab, get previous mount options from /etc/mtab if ! grep -q "$mount_point_match_regexp" /etc/fstab; then # runtime opts without some automatic kernel/userspace-added defaults previous_mount_opts=$(grep "$mount_point_match_regexp" /etc/mtab | head -1 | awk '{print $4}' \ | sed -E "s/(rw|defaults|seclabel|nodev)(,|$)//g;s/

triage_decision.reason: Adding the nodev option to the /dev/shm mount is a standard hardening step that does not affect authentication, networking, or critical services. It is a simple configuration change that can be applied without risk of lockout or system breakage.

review_feedback: The proposed script is incomplete and lacks critical safety checks. It does not backup /etc/fstab, does not verify existing entries or syntax, and does not remount /dev/shm after modification. Incorrectly editing fstab can lead to boot failure or loss of network access, potentially locking out SSH and other vital services.

previous_review_verdicts.feedback: The plan addresses the core requirement of adding the nodev option to the /dev/shm mount entry, but it would benefit from clearer handling of edge cases and safer editing of /etc/fstab.
concerns: Incomplete script excerpt—no remount or reload shown.
Potential syntax errors in sed/awk pipeline as presented.
No backup or audit of the original fstab before modification.
No verification that nodev is not already present before addition.
No validation that the mount point is actually /dev/shm when running.
Script may not work on systems where /etc/mtab is a symlink to /proc/self/mounts or absent.
No handling of SELinux context changes or permissions on /dev/shm after remount.
The mount reloading step (systemctl daemon-reload / mount -o remount) is missing.
